title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment that tested whether a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. The confirmatory design used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), a single generator/prompt pairing (requested model: gpt-5-mini), and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) running the full_intent_constraint_validation rule. Execution employed shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms) and allowed at most one bounded repair attempt per task. All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480) with model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation). Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Two preregistration/execution deviations constrain interpretation: (1) shared-generation semantics removed the per-arm stochasticity assumed by the preregistered power calculation, and (2) the prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison was not executed. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no additional verifier-detectable benefit in this executed artifact-backed setting because no verifier-detectable errors occurred; results do not generalize beyond the executed semantics, model, task bank, repair budget, or verifier.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) promise productivity gains for network operators by translating natural-language intent into device configurations, but stochastic generation can produce syntactically plausible yet semantically unsafe outputs that violate network invariants (reachability, required workflow sequences, protected interfaces). Prior work therefore recommends interposing deterministic validators and iterative repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects before execution. Empirical and method papers show improvements on syntactic or executable metrics with verifier/repair architectures, while also noting that gains on surface metrics need not imply domain-level semantic correctness for complex NetOps invariants. To provide a preregistered, artifact-backed assessment of bounded GVR in a controlled setting, we executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1) on a public synthetic NetOps task bank (240 pairs). Our primary question was whether a deterministic verifier plus at most one bounded LLM repair attempt (GVR) reduces the rate of verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to unconstrained LLM generation. Key distinguishing features of our run are: (i) a frozen preregistration and analysis executor, (ii) a deterministic pybatfish-style validator applying topology-aware rules (full_intent_constraint_validation), (iii) paired design with shared-initial-candidate generation semantics (one initial model call per task reused across arms), and (iv) bounded repair budget (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). The archived execution and analysis artifacts are the authoritative record for all numeric claims reported here.
sections.related_work: Three literature strands frame this study. First, surveys and empirical studies document hallucinations and incorrect outputs from LLMs for code and structured artifacts, motivating verifier-based pipelines to reduce operational risk. These works show that unconstrained generation can fail deeper invariants even when surface syntax looks correct. Second, methods and systems research on GVR, constrained decoding, and schema/grammar enforcement demonstrates reproducible improvements on mechanically checkable properties (e.g., syntactic validity, compilability) when validators or grammar constraints are interposed; however, these gains often focus on surface-level or executable checks rather than full domain-level semantics. Third, NetOps-specific research advocates verifier-driven evaluation, topology- and policy-aware validation, and conservative operator-in-the-loop workflows for high-stakes changes. Prior prototypes and benchmarks motivate our deferred focus on deterministic verifier predicates and paired evaluation, but they also highlight two persistent evaluation gaps: verifier completeness (oracle coverage of operational invariants) and the need for evaluation semantics that preserve per-arm generator stochasticity when measuring repair efficacy. Our design attempted to address both but executed under shared-generation semantics that removed within-pair stochastic variation, a critical distinction relative to many prior GVR case studies.
sections.methodology: Study design and preregistered estimand. The preregistered primary estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (proportion difference: GVR arm minus baseline) computed by the frozen analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). Two primary contrasts were prespecified (GVR vs unconstrained baseline; GVR vs schema-constrained decoding) with Bonferroni correction across the pair. Sampling: 12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks = 240 paired tasks (planned_episode_count = 480). Model and adapter. The run used the adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested generator gpt-5-mini with model configuration parameters recorded in the execution manifest. Important executed parameters (from archived configuration): generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false), initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (single bounded repair), and retrieval_augmented_generation = false. Deterministic verifier. The validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) implemented a pybatfish-style full_intent_constraint_validation rule set that checks required command sequences, topology-aware reachability and ACL predicates, protected-interface preservation, and final-state predicates; it returns structured diagnostics including violation_count and explicit violation lists. Task bank. The synthetic task bank encodes initial device states, natural-language intents, required_sequence constraints, and expected final states; tasks include difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count) which the validator records in its traces. Execution semantics and repair. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the adapter performed one model call per task, produced a shared_initial_candidate, and presented that same candidate to both arms; the bounded repair loop was permitted but only executed if the validator reported violations for the candidate. Analysis plan. The preregistered analysis executor conducted an exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes and computed paired absolute risk reductions with paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence intervals (bootstrap_resamples = 10,000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness and sensitivity rules were preregistered (including conservative treatments of failures as violations); the executed run produced no model-call or verifier failures.
sections.results: Execution accounting and primary outcomes. The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 240, and model_calls_used = 240 (shared-initial-candidate semantics produced one initial generation per task reused across arms). The frozen analysis executor reports baseline_success_count = 240 and guarded_success_count = 240 (baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency counts are n_11 = 240, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI (percentile; 10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Repair usage. For every episode the validator trace records repair_applied = false; the bounded repair loop never executed because the shared initial candidate satisfied all verifier predicates across the task set. Representative example. A typical task (task-000001) produced the shared initial candidate and final_configuration "interface edge1 admin down; interface edge1 vlan 30; interface edge1 mtu 1600; interface edge1 admin up"; validator traces for that task record violation_count = 0 before and after validation and repair_applied = false. Deterministic reconciliation and accounting. The deterministic_reconciliation artifact reports consistent episode accounting, provider_call_audit showing hosted_model_call_event_count = 240, cache_miss_count = 240, and stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 240; all deterministic consistency checks passed.
sections.discussion: Scientific interpretation given executed semantics. In the executed setting—single generator/prompt pairing, shared-initial-candidate semantics, synthetic task bank, single bounded repair attempt, and a deterministic verifier—bounded GVR produced no verifier-detectable benefit because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. This is a defensible, conservative interpretation of the artifact-backed null outcome: if the verifier reports zero violations for all generated candidates in both arms, there is no observable within-pair signal for the paired test to detect. Design consequences and lessons. Two evaluation-design choices determine the potential to detect GVR benefits: (1) generation semantics (shared vs independent) determine within-pair discordance potential—measuring GVR’s efficacy to correct stochastic generator errors requires independent per-condition generation; (2) verifier sensitivity and task selection (including adversarial or golden-reference injections) determine whether the task set yields verifier-detectable failures. Our preregistration assumed independent-generation for power calculations; the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated that assumption and deterministically reduced discordance potential. Likewise, the prespecified golden-injection plan (10% golden tasks) and the prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison were not realized in the archived adapter-configured run and therefore cannot be used to assess verifier sensitivity or the second primary contrast. Operational implications. Evaluators seeking to measure bounded GVR effects should (a) preserve independent_condition_generation = true to retain within-pair stochasticity; (b) include golden/adversarial items to validate verifier sensitivity; (c) consider multi-model regimes and larger repair budgets to observe iterative repair dynamics; and (d) broaden verifier coverage to reduce oracle incompleteness risk. Statistical and inferential note. The paired test is degenerate when there are zero discordant pairs: no within-pair information exists and the McNemar statistic is undefined apart from the reported p = 1.00; the bootstrap CI is also degenerate at [0.0, 0.0] because all resamples reproduce identical paired outcomes under the executed semantics. These numeric outputs faithfully reflect the frozen analysis executor’s computation on the archived data.
sections.conclusion: We performed a fully preregistered, artifact-archived paired experiment to evaluate bounded GVR for intent→configuration NetOps on a 240-pair synthetic task bank using a deterministic verifier. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier (n11 = 240), producing a degenerate paired estimate (0.0), exact McNemar p = 1.00, and paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR added no verifier-detectable value in this executed artifact-backed setting because no verifier-detectable errors occurred. Two preregistration/execution deviations constrain inference: (1) shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered independent-generation power assumption, and (2) the prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison and golden-injection checks were not executed in the archived run. The archived execution, validator traces, and analysis outputs are released as the authoritative record so others can reproducibly rerun the task bank under independent-generation semantics, inject adversarial/golden tasks, vary model scope, and expand the repair budget and verifier predicates to more robustly assess GVR’s operational value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but also removed per-arm stochastic variation and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
